messages:
noah (eng-runtime): Heads-up: after yesterday's kernel-selector + micro-batch changes, canary telemetry shows a large p95 regression for mini-burst short requests (<50 tokens). p50 unchanged but tail is noisy. Anyone looking? :grimacing:

anya (perf): saw the alert. quick numbers from canary-3: p95 40ms -> 165ms, p99 90ms -> 380ms. Throughput steady.

kai (eng-ml): did we change the metadata hashing in validate_variant? We added a few optional fields last week (quant hint + build_tag). If that made the hash non-deterministic it could trigger tokenizer rebuilds.

anya (perf): grabbed a short cpu+syscall trace. Top suspects: tokenizer allocation, repeated kv_cache lookups, and lots of small writev syscalls. pprof: internal link https://pprof.internal/canary/6290/mini-burst

anya (perf): top lines:
```
30.1% tokenize_worker
19.4% writev/syscall
12.0% kernel_selector::validate_variant
8.6% kv_cache::lookup
```

noah (eng-runtime): repro I used (local canary):
```
wrk -t8 -c180 -d45s --script=short_chat.lua http://canary-3:8080/v1/stream
```

kai (eng-ml): kv_cache metrics show more misses for small batches; micro-batching (window 3ms -> 1ms) reduced batch size so kv lookups are less amortized.

anya (perf): also noticed streaming emitter skipping MSG_MORE on a fast-path when the tokenizer pool is freshly allocated. That causes kernel to flush more often -> many small syscalls.

noah (eng-runtime): candidate fixes:
- revert kernel-selector feature flag on canary (fast)
- patch validate_variant to hash stable subset only (medium)
- avoid destroying tokenizer pool on spurious validate failures (medium)
- ensure streaming emitter always uses MSG_MORE when response incomplete (fast)

ops-bot: Initiating rollback of feature kernel-selector on canary group. Started at 09:12 UTC. Status: in-progress.

anya (perf): quick local test: forcing MSG_MORE on intermediate chunks cut syscall count ~60% and p95 back to ~55ms on repro. Patch seems low-risk but needs tests for framing.

ops-bot: Rollback completed on canary hosts. Health checks passing.

noah (eng-runtime): can confirm canary p95 back to ~52ms after rollback. Holding the rollout until we land a stable-hash + tokenizer-pool durability patch and add a perf gate.

kai (eng-ml): I'll open a PR today that restricts metadata hashing to stable fields (model_id, arch, quant_profile) and adds a unit test that simulates optional extras.

anya (perf): I'll add a short_stream perf job in CI that runs wrk + collects writev counts; fail if p95 increases >20% for short requests.

noah (eng-runtime): thanks — plan: revert done, PRs for stable-hash + MSG_MORE guard, perf job. Postmortem after fixes.
